title: From Search Tool to
AI Talent Intelligence Platform
redrob-llm.brief: Transforming a Recruiter Search Platform into an AI-Powered Professional Workspace.

cover.label: Redrob AI — From Search Tool to Talent Intelligence Platform

redrob-llm.overview: Redrob began as a single-purpose people-search tool and evolved into a connected, AI-native prospecting platform — spanning People Search, Company Search, a self-serve Developer Hub, and Redrob AI, a fully conversational LLM interface.

problemStatement.intro: The product had a single functioning feature — People Search — designed to help recruiters discover and enrich candidate profiles. This created three interconnected challenges:

challenges.v: Recruiters relied heavily on complex filter combinations to find relevant candidates, making the experience time-consuming and cognitively demanding. It required excessive manual effort before users could achieve meaningful results.

The platform was built around People Search, while customer needs had expanded beyond candidate discovery. Recruiters increasingly wanted to explore target companies and integrate Redrob into their existing workflows through APIs.
The recruitment industry was rapidly shifting toward AI-assisted experiences, where users expected to express hiring intent in natural language instead of manual filters.

problemStatement.closing: The challenge was to improve the core search experience, expand the product ecosystem with new capabilities, and increase feature adoption through better discoverability.

redrob-llm.businessGoals: The objective was to evolve Redrob from a feature-centric recruiter search tool into a scalable, AI-powered Talent Intelligence platform — and to strategically reposition Redrob for its next phase of growth.
myRoleDetail: Owned the UX strategy behind the platform evolution.
Started with auditing the existing product, running feedback loops with users and internal sales teams.
Translated findings into measurable improvements at every stage.
Defined the vision for how the product will scale with the future roadmap.
targetAudience: Founders & small-team operators doing their own outbound prospecting
Recruiters sourcing candidate pools by role, skill and company

phases.name: Optimizing the Core Experience of People Search
triggers: Time in getting results were very high.
No clear visual representation of loading activities .
High-value business data was not monetized effectively.
research: Conducted a UX audit, treating myself as a user.
Collected and analysed feedback from recruiters, sales teams, and internal stakeholders.
Ran a competitive analysis of Juicebox, Apollo, Clay, and Lusha.
decisions: Expanded search filters — decision makers, growth intent signals, separated funding and revenue signals.
Improved the results interface by clubbing action items and simplifying the UI.
Introduced feedback mechanisms — quick feedback popups and ratings.
Introduced premium filters — moved high-value filters like revenue and advanced decision-maker targeting into paid plans.

outcomes.k: Increase in Revenue by Paid Filters

phases.name: Introducing Company Search
triggers: No easy way to discover Companies matching specific business criteria.
No unified view of Companies and People while moving between multiple platforms.
research: Benchmarked comparable workflows of Apollo and Lusha to understand established mental models.
Observed that after finding a company, the next immediate task was identifying decision-makers and relevant employees.
Designed the underlying People ↔ Company relationship model in collaboration with engineering, so the two entities felt like one connected graph rather than two separate tools.
decisions: Shipped a standalone Company Search with advanced filters (industry, headcount, funding, tech stack).
Built a Company Detail Profile page summarising key account data at a glance — size, HQ location, founded year, industry.
Added a bi-directional pivot — jump from a company to its people, and from a person's card back to their company — inside a single connected flow.

outcomes.k: Faster prospect discovery through an integrated company-to-people workflow.
Reduction in search abandonment by minimizing context switching

phases.name: Developer Hub — API Keys
triggers: Enterprises wanted to integrate Redrob's people and company data directly into their internal CRMs, but there was no secure self-service way to access APIs.
There was no dedicated experience for developers to generate and manage API keys, monitor usage and credits, track enrichment requests, or access documentation.
research: Interviewed technical stakeholders, in-team developers, and enterprise prospects to understand integration expectations.
Ran a competitive analysis of developer platforms such as FullEnrich and Apollo API to understand what's important and how to showcase it.
Mapped the core flow: Generate API Key → Read Documentation → Integrate API → Monitor Usage → Track API Logs.
decisions: Designed a self-service Developer Hub with API key generation and rotation.
Built a usage dashboard surfacing credits consumed, rate limits, and call history in real time.
Added API logs & status tracking — endpoint, request method, timestamp, contact info, enrichment status, webhook status, error messages.

outcomes.k: Reduction in API onboarding time through docs & guided setup

phases.name: Redrob Chrome Extension
triggers: Recruiters spent significant time sourcing candidates on LinkedIn before switching to Redrob to enrich contact details and manage prospects.
This constant context switching fragmented the workflow: copy LinkedIn profile → open Redrob → search the same profile → enrich contact details → add to list.
research: Learned that users weren't searching directly inside Redrob — LinkedIn was their primary discovery platform, while Redrob was used for enrichment and contact discovery.
Mapped the ideal workflow: Browse LinkedIn → View Redrob Insights → Add Prospect → Auto Enrich → Sync to Redrob.
decisions: Designed a lightweight side panel that appears directly on LinkedIn profile and company pages, so users can access Redrob insights without leaving their workflow.
Enabled one-click capture of any LinkedIn profile — the extension auto-fetches profile data and prepares it for enrichment instead of manual copy-paste.

outcomes.k: Increase in prospects added to Redrob lists

phases.name: Reimagining Search with AI Query & Prompt Library
triggers: The rapid adoption of conversational AI had fundamentally changed user expectations.
Users no longer wanted to build searches manually — they wanted to simply describe what they were looking for.
research: Ran comparative usability tests — filter-first vs. prompt-first flows — with think-aloud protocols across new and existing users.
Prototyped a natural-language input that parses free text into structured, still-editable filters, preserving user trust and control.
Designed a hybrid experience supporting both interaction styles instead of replacing filters completely.
decisions: Made the prompt bar the primary entry point on People and Company Search, with manual filters kept as a visible, editable fallback rather than removed.
Parsed queries into transparent filter chips so users could see and correct exactly what the system understood.
Introduced a Prompt Library with categorised, role-specific examples (recruiter, SDR, founder, growth) users could insert and edit directly.

outcomes.k: Reduction in manual filter interactions for new users

phases.name: Redrob AI — A Fully Conversational, LLM-Based Platform
triggers: The rapid adoption of LLMs such as ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini had fundamentally changed user expectations.
Users expected AI to understand natural language, reason across multiple datasets, and provide answers instead of requiring manual navigation.
research: Partnered cross-functionally with AI/ML and Product to define a conversational information architecture that could hold context across turns.
Designed how structured data (people/company cards, tables) renders legibly inside a chat-shaped interface — it could not become a wall of text.
decisions: Built an MCP-based search architecture allowing users to enable different data sources before initiating a search.

Designed a conversational search experience — instead of manually selecting People Search or Company Search, users simply describe their objective, and the AI interprets intent, selects the appropriate sources, applies relevant filters behind the scenes, and returns structured results.

outcomes.k: Faster time to discover relevant people and companies
User engagement through conversational, context-aware interactions

title: AI-powered creative platform that unified 30+ fragmented image editing workflows into one intelligent workspace.
phot-ai.brief: Phot AI enables creators, marketers, and businesses to generate, edit, enhance, and publish visual content using AI. As Product Designer, I led the end-to-end UX—from research and information architecture to interaction design and design system—to simplify complex AI workflows into a seamless creative experience.

sections.body: Creators and businesses spend significant time switching between multiple AI tools to complete a single creative task. This fragmented workflow increases production time, introduces unnecessary complexity, and makes AI adoption difficult for non-designers.
sections.body2: How Might We — create impactful creatives in less time?

sections.body: Phot AI is one-stop automation hub which eliminates the need for switching between different websites/tools, streamlining the creative process and boosting productivity. It provides 30+ features where user can do multiple tasks at one place only like background replacer, avatar generator, banner creation, photo editing tools like photo enhancer, blur background, image restoration and many more.  It is AI-powered design ecosystem where users get high quality results generated through AI.

The goal was to design a unified AI-powered platform that enables users to create, edit, enhance, and export professional-quality visual assets from one workspace.The experience needed to: Reduce workflow fragmentation, increase trust in AI-generated results, improve creative efficiency, and support users with different levels of design expertise
The project was divided into five phases:

Before defining the experience, I wanted to understand how users currently interacted with AI creative tools and where their workflows were breaking down.The research focused on identifying behavioural patterns instead of validating assumptions. Research methods included:User Interviews, Competitive Analysis, Persona Creation

items: Small Business Owners - Need professional product visuals quickly without hiring designers.
Professional Designers - Require AI as a productivity tool rather than a replacement for creativity.
Everyday Users - Want simple editing tools for personal images without learning professional software.
How users currently create visual content
Which AI tools they combine during one workflow
Where they lose the most time
How much creative control users expect

sections.body: I audited 14 tools spanning general creative AI (Canva, Adobe Firefly, Midjourney, DALL·E), ad-specific generators (Pencil, Smartly, Predis) and more, to understand where existing products stopped short. Most tools optimised for a single step in the workflow — generation, or editing, or publishing — but none closed the loop between what creative was produced and how it actually performed in market.

Mapping what users said, thought, and felt surfaced a consistent tension: marketers said they wanted 'more AI features,' but what they actually felt was anxiety about defending an AI decision they couldn't explain. The real gap wasn't capability — it was confidence. Every interface decision after this point was filtered through one question: does this make the AI's reasoning visible enough for a non-designer to trust and defend it?
Labeled cards into categories according to own understanding and sorting it wisely.
This user flow is of a tool named BG replacer which takes user from starting point through a set of steps till the final output.

breakdown.title: AI Art Generator
breakdown.subtext: Turn simple text prompts into production-ready artwork in seconds. Explore multiple artistic styles, generate high-quality visuals, and accelerate creative exploration with AI-powered image generation.

breakdown.title: Dashboard
breakdown.subtext: A unified creative workspace for designing, editing, and managing visual assets. From templates and brand kits to AI-powered editing, every tool is organized into a streamlined workflow.

breakdown.title: AI Background Replacer
breakdown.subtext: Remove and replace backgrounds with a single click using AI. Generate clean, professional product visuals and lifestyle imagery without complex editing or manual masking.

breakdown.title: Phot AI Magic Studio
breakdown.subtext: An all-in-one mobile editing studio combining AI-powered creation, image enhancement, color adjustments, brush tools, and effects into a seamless creative workflow from start to finish.

sections.body: This project fundamentally changed how I think about designing AI-powered products. I realized that users aren't looking for more AI features — they're looking for confidence that the product will help them achieve their goals without adding complexity. The real design challenge wasn't exposing advanced capabilities, but making sophisticated technology feel approachable, transparent, and reliable.

title: Designing the Official Digital
Ecosystem for a New Cricket League
bcl.brief: Designing an end-to-end mobile ecosystem for a new professional T20 cricket tournament — from live scores and fan communities to a paid Fan Ownership commerce layer.

cover.label: Big Cricket League — Designing the Official Digital Ecosystem

sections.body: Big Cricket League (BCL) launched as a new professional T20 cricket tournament featuring international legends and emerging talent. The goal was to design an end-to-end mobile ecosystem that would become the primary digital destination for cricket fans around the tournament — live scores and commentary, team and player stats, standings, news, video content — and a deeper, paid affiliation layer called Fan Ownership, where a fan can buy into a team and unlock benefits and exclusive community access.

Unlike IPL and other established cricket tournaments that have mature digital products, Big Cricket League had no official application to support fans before, during, or after matches. The absence of a centralized platform fragmented the entire fan journey. The key challenges were identified across the following areas:

items.v: Cricket fans relied on multiple third-party platforms such as Cricbuzz, Google, YouTube, Instagram, and news websites to follow a single tournament.

items.k: Lack of a Centralized Information Hub
items.v: Tournament-related information was scattered across different channels with no official source providing complete coverage.

items.k: Poor Fan Engagement Beyond Match Days
items.v: User engagement was largely limited to live broadcasts. Once a match ended, there was little reason for fans to continue interacting with the league.
The platform lacked features that encouraged fans to actively participate rather than passively consume content. There was no ecosystem for Fan ownership, Team communities, Fan loyalty.

sections.body: Rather than building another score-tracking app, the objective was to create a digital ecosystem capable of supporting the complete fan lifecycle. The platform needed to:
items: Improve fan retention
Build a loyal digital community
Establish Big Cricket League's own digital identity
Give all franchises a consistent home inside one platform instead of fragmented team-level presences

sections.body: With no budget in this phase for direct fan interviews, the process leaned on three inputs instead of one:

items.v: Reviewed existing league apps like IPL, Cricbuzz, cricket score/stats aggregators and fantasy platforms to establish what a strong baseline experience looks like for live score, commentary and stats.

Used well-established patterns in how sports fans actually behave — checking score compulsively during play, reacting in the moment, wanting recognition for loyalty — as design inputs in place of direct interviews.

The league's own commercial goals — sponsor visibility, and specifically the Fan Ownership commerce model — shaped scope directly and were translated into designed flows rather than emerging from user research.

sections.body: Based on insights gathered from stakeholder discussions, competitive analysis, and product research, a comprehensive Product Requirements Document (PRD) was created by the Product Manager. The PRD served as the single source of truth, consolidating business objectives, user needs, feature requirements, functional specifications, success metrics, and project scope. This ensured alignment across product, design, and engineering teams before moving into the design phase.

The sitemap organises into eight pillars, all reachable from a deliberately minimal four-item bottom navigation (Home, Fan Club, Videos, More) that pushes secondary destinations into an overflow rather than trying to surface everything at once.

breakdown.title: Transforming fans into Team Owners
breakdown.subtext: Designed an end-to-end ownership journey that enables fans to discover teams, purchase ownership, manage memberships, unlock exclusive benefits, and access ownership documents through a seamless experience.

breakdown.title: A Central hub for the entire cricket league
breakdown.subtext: Designed a unified league experience where fans can seamlessly explore tournament standings, player leaderboards, galleries, venue information, sponsors, and league-wide updates from a single destination.

breakdown.title: Building rich digital identities for every player
breakdown.subtext: Designed comprehensive player profiles that combine statistics, achievements, awards, news, and career milestones, helping fans discover players beyond their on-field performance.

sections.body: Created a prototype for each feature & shared with the developers and stakeholders to review. Feedback given was that design was very intuitive and easy to use.

title: Designing a Storytelling Platform
for an 80-Year Legacy Restaurant
pritam.brief: An immersive digital experience for one of Mumbai's most iconic restaurants — where every section tells a meaningful part of Pritam's 80-year journey, since 1942.

sections.body: Pritam Restaurant has been one of Mumbai's most iconic dining destinations since 1942, and the restaurant credited with introducing butter chicken to Mumbai. Over four generations, it built a genuine Bollywood-era legacy: Raj Kapoor inaugurated its first outlet in 1975, and many actors including Sunil Dutt, Dilip Kumar, Dharmendra and Sunil Gavaskar visited. The business now also runs Pritam Da Dhaba, a related but distinct concept with an original outlet in Dadar and a newer one in Juhu aimed at a younger audience.
sections.body2: Instead of designing a conventional restaurant website, the goal was to create an immersive digital experience where every section tells a meaningful part of Pritam's journey.

items: New visitors had no way to discover its history.
International audiences couldn't understand its cultural significance.
Customers couldn't explore its legacy before visiting.
The brand had no digital platform to preserve and communicate stories accumulated over generations.
Legacy storytelling
Visual gallery
Experience the menu
Identified the problem
Found out solutions
Documented the important things to showcase
Started with moodboarding, wireframes, and design system
Figma designs and prototype
Developer handoff

breakdown.title: Setting the stage before the first scroll
breakdown.subtext: The experience begins with a bilingual animated introduction, first revealing the brand in English, followed by Hindi, reflecting Pritam's deep-rooted identity and its connection with generations of visitors. The animation seamlessly transitions into the hero section with the message 80 rs of Continuity, immediately communicating the restaurant's remarkable legacy before users begin exploring the website.

breakdown.title: 80 Years of Culinary Legacy
breakdown.subtext: The hero section establishes authenticity by showcasing the original restaurant branding and visual elements inspired by its early identity. Rather than introducing the restaurant with marketing copy, the design highlights its 80-year journey, allowing visitors to instantly recognize Pritam as one of Mumbai's oldest and most iconic dining destinations.

breakdown.title: Celebrating decades of cultural connections
breakdown.subtext: As an iconic restaurant in Mumbai, Pritam has been visited by generations of Bollywood celebrities and renowned personalities. This section showcases archival photographs to celebrate these associations, adding credibility while creating an emotional connection with visitors. The visual storytelling reinforces Pritam's cultural significance and highlights its place in Mumbai's cinematic history.

breakdown.title: Preserving moments beyond the plate
breakdown.subtext: To bring the restaurant's atmosphere to life, an interactive gallery showcases interiors, signature dishes, memorable moments, and historic photographs. Instead of simply displaying images, the gallery helps visitors experience Pritam's warmth, heritage, and vibrant dining culture, making it easier for them to connect with the brand before visiting.

sections.body: The final product is not simply a restaurant website. It is a digital museum, a brand archive, and a storytelling platform that allows visitors to experience more than eighty years of culinary heritage before they ever step inside the restaurant.
sections.body2: By structuring the experience around stories rather than pages, the website transforms Pritam's history into an engaging digital journey while creating a scalable foundation for future growth, locations, and brand storytelling.

title: Privacy, finally
feels effortless.
pulpy-vpn.brief: Pulpy VPN is a mobile VPN application designed to make secure browsing feel approachable rather than technical. Unlike conventional VPN products that focus purely on functionality, the goal was to create a friendly experience using a mascot-driven visual language while maintaining usability across onboarding, subscriptions, connectivity states, and engagement touchpoints.

sections.body: VPN applications are generally perceived as technical products filled with server lists, networking terminology, and security jargon. The product team wanted Pulpy VPN to feel:
items: Friendly
Easy for first-time users
Visually memorable
Consumer privacy market

sections.body: This project was primarily focused on UI execution and flow design.I worked closely with the Product Manager who defined product requirements and feature priorities. My responsibilities included:
items: Translating requirements into wireframes
Designing complete mobile UI
Creating interaction flows,mascot illustrations and promotional cards
Preparing developer handoff in Figma

sections.body: The design process which I followed was very simple but fully focused on better user experience.
One of the most distinctive parts of the project was designing a mascot that could communicate different product states throughout the application.

breakdown.title: 3-screen onboarding
breakdown.subtext: Designed a lightweight onboarding experience introducing key product capabilities. The objective was to communicate value quickly without overwhelming new users.

breakdown.title: Subscription Experience
breakdown.subtext: Designed the premium upgrade flow including: Pricing plans, membership confirmation, upgrade success, subscription cancellation. The layouts emphasized clear pricing, benefits, and strong visual hierarchy.

breakdown.title: 'Network & Error States
breakdown.subtext: Created illustrations and UI for different connectivity scenarios including: No Internet, retry states, connection failures. Instead of generic system messages, the mascot helped make these states more approachable while still communicating the issue clearly.

breakdown.title: Promotional Cards
breakdown.subtext: Designed reusable marketing cards for:Referral rewards, free data, subscription offers, and user engagement campaigns. These components were created for use across the application without requiring separate visual assets each time.

breakdown.title: Email Templates
breakdown.subtext: Designed responsive email templates for: Login links, account communication and brand consistency. The templates followed the same visual language as the mobile application to provide a cohesive user experience across touchpoints.

sections.body: After completing the visual design, assets were organized inside Figma for developer implementation.Deliverables included:
items: Component-based screens
Export-ready illustrations
Developer specifications

sections.body: 100K downloads. 88-second onboarding. 4.2★ Play Store. 3.2× conversion.

items.v: 100K+ in the first 6 months post-launch, across India and Southeast Asia
88 seconds, app open → first protected state, across all tested device tiers
3.2× improvement with mid-use paywall vs. the original end-of-trial placement
4.2★ from organic reviews — highest-rated theme: 'simple to use'

sections.body: This project reinforced that visual design plays a significant role in shaping how users perceive technical products. Some key takeaways included:
items: Using illustrations and mascots to make functional interfaces feel more approachable.
Designing reusable components that improve scalability and developer efficiency.
Collaborating closely with product managers and developers to move designs efficiently from concept to implementation.
Building a memorable product identity through consistent visual language.
